candidates.summary: Michael Mullins' family recall a devoted dad while colleagues describe how he helped transform a school

candidates.lead: Michael Mullins' family recall a devoted dad while colleagues describe how he helped transform a school
candidates.evidence_text: Michael Mullins: Family remember 'irreplaceable' head teacher - BBC News Image source, Family handout Image caption, Michael Mullins was described by his wife as "irreplaceable to family, friends, and the school" By Haider Saleem North West Published 2 November 2026 "Michael was my safety net," said Sarah Mullins as she described the loss of her husband, a head teacher who was murdered while cycling home from work. Michael Mullins, 56, loved music, was learning to play the guitar and would collect his daughter and her friends from concerts to make sure they got home safely. Colleagues said he had transformed Stretford Grammar School in Trafford, Greater Manchester, after becoming head teacher in 2009, when it was in special measures, and that his death had left "a void at every level". The tributes were heard at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court as Simon Richardson, 35, was jailed for life with a minimum term of 25 years for murdering Mr Mullins on 20 April. Warning: This article contains distressing content Richardson struck Mr Mullins with his car in Warburton, Greater Manchester, before driving for more than a mile with the injured cyclist trapped underneath. Sarah described the many roles her husband had played in family life. "Michael was a cook, chauffeur, finance expert, quick to laugh and generous with time and money," she told Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court. "My past, present, and future have been brutally and callously torn apart." Image source, Family handout Image caption, Michael Mullins with his children, Harry and Maisie, who remembered him as a devoted father who always made time for them Their son, Harry, described his father as his best friend. "Dad wanted to make the world a better place," he said. "He was the type of dad who would show up to everything." Mr Mullins's daughter, Maisie, described him as "the hardest-working person I have ever and will ever know". She said her father had at least nine years before retirement and reflected on the generations of pupils who would now miss out on his leadership. "That is nine cohorts that have been deprived of him," she said. 'Bound together by him' Mr Mullins became head teacher of Stretford Grammar School in 2009, when it was in special measures, the court heard. Acting head Elizabeth Baxter described his impact as "truly transformative" and said he was determined to raise standards and expectations. She credited Mr Mullins with securing a new school building project and said he had wanted more pupils from disadvantaged backgrounds to have the opportunity to attend. Ms Baxter said colleagues now found it "unbearably sad" to attend meetings about the building project without him. "As a community, not just led by Michael but bound together by him, his death was devastating," she said. "I saw students and staff in tears. Students became accustomed to seeing their teachers in tears." Image source, Family handout Image caption, Mullins had led Stretford Grammar School since 2009 and was credited with transforming it Flowers were laid outside the school, with some people climbing the gates to leave tributes after it had closed. At his funeral, mourners stood outside in the pouring rain to pay their respects, Ms Baxter said. "Michael had a reach and an impact which stretched far beyond our school gates," she said. But it was also in the familiar routines of school life that his absence continued to be felt. "Students don't have him standing on the front gate any longer. The staff don't have him in his office anymore with the door open," Ms Baxter said. candidates.lead: Greater Manchester's Metrolink tram network will still be subject to some minor route changes
candidates.evidence_text: Tram services were running as normal on Greater Manchester's Metrolink network again on Monday after two weeks of major disruption Improvement works have taken place at Deansgate-Castlefield and Trafford Bar, as well as in Manchester city centre, meaning no services ran on three Metrolink lines over that time A spokesman for Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) confirmed the work was on schedule to have been completed However, passengers have been warned that some minor route changes through the city centre will remain in place until Wednesday, with travellers advised to check the TfGM website , external Vernon Everitt, Greater Manchester's transport commissioner, told BBC Radio Manchester 's Hot Seat programme the works would be "the last big closures for a while" "Unfortunately there's never a good time to do these closures and I do apologise, but everyone will reap the benefits of it."

candidates.lead: Courts "We are completely adrift and bereft without our anchor, Michael Mullins" Simon Richardson was jailed for life for the murder of Michael Mullins Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 19:30, 02 Nov 2026 Updated 06:55, 03 Nov 20 In a packed public gallery
candidates.evidence_text: Courts "We are completely adrift and bereft without our anchor, Michael Mullins" Simon Richardson was jailed for life for the murder of Michael Mullins Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 19:30, 02 Nov 2026 Updated 06:55, 03 Nov 20 In a packed public gallery, full of close friends, family members and colleagues of the late Michael Mullins, his wife, Sarah spoke with dignity and grace Her husband, the beloved and revered headteacher of Stretford Grammar school, had been killed as he was cycling home from work. His killer, Simon Richardson, struck Mr Mullins at the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane in Partington, on April 20 this year Mr Mullins was then dragged underneath Richardson's Volvo for 2.2km - or 1.3 miles - before dying at the roadside on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm. Minshull Street Crown Court heard that Richardson had previously made 'physical concerted efforts' to remove Mr Mullins from under his car b Richardson, 35, then drove away from the scene, later swapping his car for a silver van. The following day he was finally caught up with after leading police on a high speed pursuit through Failsworth Following a two week trial, jurors found him guilty of murder and dangerous driving. Today, November 2, he was jailed for life to serve a minimum term of 25 years

Mr Burnham was then collected at Manchester along with his wife, Ma Former prime minister Gordon Brown was also on the Government plane. The Guido Fawkes website estimated the cost of the Stansted-Manchester flight as £20,000 But the Prime Minister's spokesperson defended the decision and said security, operational reasons and value for money for the taxpayer were all considerations when deciding on how the Prime Minster travels. The spokesperson said: “The Prime Minister’s travel arrangements are mad "The Prime Minister’s travel arrangements reflect where he was carrying out official government business at the end of last week. He spent the day in Scotland on Friday, returned to Manchester to work from Number 10 North on Friday evening.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Wigan dad, 42, dies in devastating fire weeks after his home is turned into 'bomb site' by 'invaders' Mark Venal died in hospital Add to preferred sources News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 06:05, 03 Nov 2026 Updated 07:14, 03 Nov 2026 View 3 Im A beloved dad-of-two who tragically died in a house fire was ‘invaded’ months before his death, an inquest heard. Mark Vernal sadly died in hospital after he was trapped in a blaze at his family home on Dumbarton Green in Wigan on August 14, 2024 An inquest into his death began at Bolton Coroners Court on Monday (November 2) Several members of Mark’s family attended the court, including representatives of Greater Manchester Police and Wigan Council. Among Mark's family was his brother and sister, Michael and Sonia Vernal The pair told the court how they believed Mark was a victim of ‘cuckooing’ in the lead up to his death. Cuckooing is when criminals take control of a vulnerable person’s home to use it for crime "A lot of people take advantage of him that way," said his brother, Michael. "He was really vulnerable and a lot more when he was under the influence."

candidates.evidence_text: Courts "We are completely adrift and bereft without our anchor, Michael Mullins" Simon Richardson was jailed for life for the murder of Michael Mullins Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 19:30, 02 Nov 2026 Updated 06:55, 03 Nov 20 In a packed public gallery, full of close friends, family members and colleagues of the late Michael Mullins, his wife, Sarah spoke with dignity and grace Her husband, the beloved and revered headteacher of Stretford Grammar school, had been killed as he was cycling home from work. His killer, Simon Richardson, struck Mr Mullins at the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane in Partington, on April 20 this year Mr Mullins was then dragged underneath Richardson's Volvo for 2.2km - or 1.3 miles - before dying at the roadside on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm. Minshull Street Crown Court heard that Richardson had previously made 'physical concerted efforts' to remove Mr Mullins from under his car b Richardson, 35, then drove away from the scene, later swapping his car for a silver van. The following day he was finally caught up with after leading police on a high speed pursuit through Failsworth Following a two week trial, jurors found him guilty of murder and dangerous driving. Today, November 2, he was jailed for life to serve a minimum term of 25 years

candidates.lead: Was Shabana Mahmood forced into a U-turn over her migrant reforms?
candidates.evidence_text: Was Shabana Mahmood forced into a U-turn over her migrant reforms? The Home Secretary has watered down her plans to make foreign care workers wait 15 years for settlement. But was it down to her own sense of "fairness" or did she capitulate to other C On Monday afternoon, Shabana Mahmood addressed the Commons by discussing a deeply personal account of her own family’s migration to the UK 50 years ago from rural Kashmir “They came here knowing one thing above all else – that they would be treated fairly here,” she told Parliament. “They came from a place where power was often arbitrary and where the dice were always loaded. They came to this country because they knew we do things differently her It was an appeal to the values the Home Secretary believes underpins Britain’s immigration system – a sense of fairness Ms Mahmood reiterated those views when she announced her reforms on migration She said a five-year path to settlement will remain open for those earning over £50,000, and those earning 125,000 would get a fast-track route to settlement after just three years

candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police New arrest made in 'HMO' attacks probe after properties targeted across Greater Manchester A total of eight people have now been detained following spate of vandalism across Greater Manchester Add to preferred sources News Da Police have made another arrest as a probe into a spate of vandalism and criminal damage against HMOs across Greater Manchester continues. Greater Manchester Police launched an investigation into dozens of suspected incidents across Salford , Tameside , Bolton , Rochdale , Wigan The force said previously it had received 46 reports of criminal damage to properties that are either houses of multiple occupation, or properties being mistaken for HMOs, since October 5. In some of the incidents, homes had 'no HMO' sprayed onto their front doors Cars were also smashed and windows broken. This morning (Monday) a 29-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage in connection with the attacks Chief Supt Marcus Noden previously said police believe that vulnerable people, including children, have been exploited and paid to damage buildings. He said: "Our relentless pursuit of those causing or facilitating this recent spate of damage is not letting up as we continue to e "One area of focus continues to be our belief that vulnerable people - including children - are being exploited and paid to damage buildings. If you know anything that could help us, we're continuing to urge you to come forward and speak to us

candidates.summary: Rochdale Banned driver led police on high-speed chase through the streets of Rochdale Bilal Ishaq reached speeds more than three times the limit as he tried to outrun police motorcyclists in a black Mercedes Add to preferred sources News Damon Wilkins Police footage shows officer

candidates.evidence_text: Rochdale Banned driver led police on high-speed chase through the streets of Rochdale Bilal Ishaq reached speeds more than three times the limit as he tried to outrun police motorcyclists in a black Mercedes Add to preferred sources News Damon Wilkins Police footage shows officers take up the pursuit on Foxholes Road after they suspected the 35-year-old of drug dealing. In the clip an officer can be heard saying 'It's a black Mercedes, believe he's drug dealing' Ishaq can then be seen racing through residential streets at speeds of over 60mph. At one point he goes through a mini-roundabout on the wrong side of the road, narrowly avoiding a car pulling out from a side street He also ran red lights and twice attempted to reverse into the police riders. As the pursuit comes to an end he pulls over and attempts to run away, as the abandoned Mercedes rolls down the street with the drivers door still open Ishaq, of Hey Street, Rochdale, who was already serving two court-imposed driving bans following a separate dangerous driving offence in December 2025, was arrested shortly afterwards He later admitted dangerous driving, driving whilst disqualified, failing to stop and driving without insurance and was jailed for 16 months and disqualified from driving for five years

Minshull Street Crown Court heard that Richardson had previously made 'physical concerted efforts' to remove Mr Mullins from under his car b Richardson, 35, then drove away from the scene, later swapping his car for a silver van. The following day he was finally caught up with after leading police on a high speed pursuit through Failsworth Following a two week trial, jurors found him guilty of murder and dangerous driving. Today, November 2, he was jailed for life to serve a minimum term of 25 years

There have been number of complaints about teenagers causing trouble around Greenfield in recent days and weeks The problems have centred around Tesco car park and the supermarket entrance on Wellington Road, officers say. candidates.evidence_text: Was Shabana Mahmood forced into a U-turn over her migrant reforms? The Home Secretary has watered down her plans to make foreign care workers wait 15 years for settlement. But was it down to her own sense of "fairness" or did she capitulate to other C On Monday afternoon, Shabana Mahmood addressed the Commons by discussing a deeply personal account of her own family’s migration to the UK 50 years ago from rural Kashmir “They came here knowing one thing above all else – that they would be treated fairly here,” she told Parliament. “They came from a place where power was often arbitrary and where the dice were always loaded. They came to this country because they knew we do things differently her It was an appeal to the values the Home Secretary believes underpins Britain’s immigration system – a sense of fairness Ms Mahmood reiterated those views when she announced her reforms on migration She said a five-year path to settlement will remain open for those earning over £50,000, and those earning 125,000 would get a fast-track route to settlement after just three years

candidates.evidence_text: Rochdale Banned driver led police on high-speed chase through the streets of Rochdale Bilal Ishaq reached speeds more than three times the limit as he tried to outrun police motorcyclists in a black Mercedes Add to preferred sources News Damon Wilkins Police footage shows officers take up the pursuit on Foxholes Road after they suspected the 35-year-old of drug dealing. In the clip an officer can be heard saying 'It's a black Mercedes, believe he's drug dealing' Ishaq can then be seen racing through residential streets at speeds of over 60mph. At one point he goes through a mini-roundabout on the wrong side of the road, narrowly avoiding a car pulling out from a side street He also ran red lights and twice attempted to reverse into the police riders. As the pursuit comes to an end he pulls over and attempts to run away, as the abandoned Mercedes rolls down the street with the drivers door still open Ishaq, of Hey Street, Rochdale, who was already serving two court-imposed driving bans following a separate dangerous driving offence in December 2025, was arrested shortly afterwards He later admitted dangerous driving, driving whilst disqualified, failing to stop and driving without insurance and was jailed for 16 months and disqualified from driving for five years

Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

Lowry to life in an innovative new production to commemorate the 50 th anniversary of his death. Matchstalks Remastered offers audiences an imaginative new way to experience the work and legacy of renowned artist L.S. Lowry. Academics Michael Pinchbeck and Kevin Egan will take to the stage for the one-night performance on November 4. Commissioned by Word of Warning and The Lowry, the production combines theatre, music and visual art in a playful exploration of the artist’s work and cultural influence. The show marks the first collaboration between Pinchbeck and Egan. Inspired by Matchstalk Men and Matchstalk Cats and Dogs, the 1978 song about Lowry, the production transforms the song into a theatrical score that guides every aspect of the performance. Pinchbeck, Professor of Theatre, said: “Matchstalks Remastered is the culmination of three years research exploring how to stage popular music and painting. We have created a score based on the famous song by Brian and Michael and mapped it onto Lowry’s iconic paintings – the resulting performance is a rich tapestry weaving together archival footage and art history, stories about Lowry and the people and places he painted, and images and motifs from the music he inspired. We are excited about premiering it at Lowry to mark this anniversary.” The show follows two performers as they attempt to keep pace with a continuously scrolling score that dictates their movement, dialogue and action. Joined on stage by a live accordion player, they navigate a world of humorous stories while transforming into a range of characters, including Lowry himself, the songwriters and figures from the artist’s paintings. Drawing on archive material provided through the North West Film Archive , the production uses Lowry’s paintings as a visual roadmap throughout the performance. Audiences will gain fresh insight into Lowry’s work and the distinctive way he viewed the industrial landscapes of northern England. Egan, Senior Lecture in Contemporary Performance, said: “For this project, Brian and Michael’s song became the blueprint for everything we built on stage, organised through a live visual score that the audience can see unfolding in real time. I’m interested in how music, theatre and even Lowry’s paintings can all be understood as systems of rhythm, repetition and compositional logic, and how those structures, when translated into a score that guides our creative decisions, are perceived as restrictive or liberating elements depending on how we process the world around us. “I enjoy seeing how Michael and I negotiate the score in the moment of performance and, like Lowry, while some might see it as a bleak and oppressive landscape, I see it as a form of beauty, vitality and possibility.” The production also showcases the work of Manchester Met alumna Rebecca Horswill, who has created original animations that bring elements of Lowry’s paintings to life on screen throughout the show. Horswill studied BA Drama and Contemporary Performance at Manchester Met, where she experimented with animation alongside creating live performances. This led her to completing a MA Animation degree and creating many animated pieces for organisations across the country. Horswill said: “From crowded busy scenes to the wag of a dog’s tail, I became truly consumed by L.S. Lowry’s world and the narrative-driven paintings. candidates.evidence_text: How a sweatshop empire is Manchester-washing its reputation “I can’t always be in LA,” reads one TikTok caption, “someone has to hold it down in Rochdale.” It’s written over a model strutting through a leatherwear shoot. She’s wearing Musera, which looks to be Manchester’s friendliest, chicest new clothing label — launched in 2024 from an From this Newton Street office, a band of young designers turn out a stream of trend pieces: low-rise trousers and asymmetric tops, distressed knitwear and leopard-print flares, western fringed jumpers and A-level prom gowns. Their Instagram bio lauds the brand as “Est. MCR.” Over a million people watched the staff dancing around their Northern Quarter office to Whigfield’s Saturday Night on TikTok. More still tuned in to a video showing them kitted out in Musera for Drake’s performance at Co-op Live last year. And who knows how many have sidestepped “Be a muse in your own era,” goes their slogan; presumably also the source of their similarly recondite name. Their Instagram captions are a list of internet cliches verging on parody. “My blood type is iced latte,” reads one post Looking at this well-curated online presence, you might well be convinced that Musera is, as they suggest, Manchester through and through

candidates.evidence_text: An 'unparalleled' investigation shows a third of staff surveyed have experienced bad behaviour from senior officials A scathing report into Manchester City Council's working culture has found a prevailing “boys' club” mentality and widespread bad behaviour by senior staff. The internal document – that will be shared with council workers tomorrow and is based on a survey of nearly 1,200 staff – The report describes a culture at the council in which senior staff can act inappropriately with seeming impunity. Many junior staff members believe raising issues will lead to retaliation, and 59% of survey respondents have witnessed or experienced a form of harassment, discrimi One worker recalled a young apprentice being repeatedly sexually harassed by a senior colleague until she was forced to leave the council. “He was allowed to stay,” they said of the offending staffer. “She was interviewed by two male managers and needless to say she left.” There A council worker, speaking to us on the condition of anonymity, said of the report: “if I were a manager that would sicken me to my core.” When we approached the council before publishing this story, CEO Tom Stannard said: “it is completely unacceptable that anyone should feel undervalued, unable to raise concerns, unsupported if they do or – in the worst cases – unsafe. These issues cannot and will not be ignored.”

candidates.lead: Manchester hospitals have become a focal point not only for improving people’s health but supporting them overcome financial or housing challenges
candidates.evidence_text: Manchester hospitals have become a focal point not only for improving people’s health but supporting them overcome financial or housing challenges In December 2023 a trial was launched to embed two Citizens Advice case workers in two Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) run hospitals in Manchester - the Royal Manchester Children's Hospital and North Manchester General Hospital This was further expanded in June 2024 to include Wythenshawe Hospital, and the MRI in March 2025, and St Mary's in December 2025 with funding through MFT’s charity, as well as a damp and mould focused case worker funded through Manchester City Council The team of six Citizens Advice caseworkers are aimed at providing better wrap around care for patients and addressing the link we know exists between poor health, economic hardship and housing issues The trial has been a huge success with more than 1,500 people supported across the trial locations With more up to 3m patients contacts across MFT each year this presented a huge opportunity to reach people who may otherwise have not known about the services provided by Citizens Advice, or the support they were eligible to claim

candidates.lead: Primary schools have been recognised for outstanding performance in the 2026 Summer Reading Challenge Read to the Beat
candidates.evidence_text: Primary schools have been recognised for outstanding performance in the 2026 Summer Reading Challenge Read to the Beat. The challenge, delivered by The Reading Agency in partnership with public libraries, encouraged children to discover the joy of reading through the theme Read to the Beat, celebrating music, rhythm and the power of stories. Royton Hall Primary School, St Martin’s Primary School and Greenfield Primary School were recognised as the schools with the highest participation out of 92 schools taking part across Oldham. Representatives from Oldham Libraries and partner Kajima, which supports opportunities to encourage children to read and celebrate their success, visited each school to award book tokens in recognition of pupils’ commitment to reading. Kajima have sponsored the Summer Reading Challenge for the sixth year running, encouraging Oldham children towards a lifelong love of books. The challenge highlights the importance of partnerships between schools, libraries and local organisations in supporting children’s literacy, building reading confidence and making reading an exciting and rewarding experience. Suzanne Hudson, Senior Development Officer for Oldham Heritage, Libraries and Arts said, “It’s fantastic to see so many children across Oldham getting involved in this year’s Summer Reading Challenge. "Reading helps children build confidence, develop their imaginations and discover a lifelong love of books. "We’re delighted to recognise Royton Hall Primary, St Martin’s Primary and Greenfield Primary for their fantastic participation, and we’re incredibly grateful to Kajima for sponsoring the challenge and helping us celebrate the children’s achievements.” Oldham Libraries would also like to thank all participating schools for their support and enthusiasm in helping to make this year’s challenge a success. There’s a warm welcome waiting for you at your local library, with free access to books, fun activities, reading and writing groups and much more to help children to fall in love with reading. Find out more here

candidates.lead: Get ready for a spooky spectacle packed with jaw-dropping performances
candidates.evidence_text: Get ready for a spooky spectacle packed with jaw-dropping performances. Prepare to be wowed in town this Saturday, with an evening packed with entertainment from 5.30pm to 7.30pm. The free event, as part of Oldham's year as the Greater Manchester Town of Culture, will transform Parliament Square into a spook-tacular Halloween and Bonfire Night-inspired celebration with jaw-dropping fiery performances and roaming characters. Visitors can experience the thrills of Juggling Inferno, the spectacular fire and pyrotechnic displays of Helter Skelter Arts, and The Lips Halloween Show. There will also be the chance to come face-to-face with Bessemer the fire-breathing dragon and Toni the giant bat, building towards a breathtaking fireworks display providing a spectacular finale to the celebrations. The stunning show by Helter Skelter Arts features tight choreography and big fire special effects. This mesmerising duo will dance with the flames, creating a display full of emotion and creativity. Juggling Inferno is a beautifully choreographed fire display featuring world class fire entertainers, and the Lips Halloween Show is a big pop-puppetry singalong with something to say. To make it easier for families to enjoy the festivities, there's free parking in all council town centre car parks from 3.30pm. Oldham Council's Director of Communities Neil Consterdine said: "The Feast of Fire is one of the most exciting events in our calendar during Oldham's year as the Greater Manchester Town of Culture — and it's completely free. "We're looking forward to welcoming families or an unforgettable evening of entertainment, and with free parking from 3.30pm, it's the perfect opportunity to come into town, enjoy the Halloween night fun and support our local businesses while you're here." For more information about the Feast of Fire

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Get ready for a spooky spectacle packed with jaw-dropping performances. Prepare to be wowed in town this Saturday, with an evening packed with entertainment from 5.30pm to 7.30pm. The free event, as part of Oldham's year as the Greater Manchester Town of Culture, will transform Parliament Square into a spook-tacular Halloween and Bonfire Night-inspired celebration with jaw-dropping fiery performances and roaming characters. Visitors can experience the thrills of Juggling Inferno, the spectacular fire and pyrotechnic displays of Helter Skelter Arts, and The Lips Halloween Show. There will also be the chance to come face-to-face with Bessemer the fire-breathing dragon and Toni the giant bat, building towards a breathtaking fireworks display providing a spectacular finale to the celebrations. The stunning show by Helter Skelter Arts features tight choreography and big fire special effects. This mesmerising duo will dance with the flames, creating a display full of emotion and creativity. Juggling Inferno is a beautifully choreographed fire display featuring world class fire entertainers, and the Lips Halloween Show is a big pop-puppetry singalong with something to say. To make it easier for families to enjoy the festivities, there's free parking in all council town centre car parks from 3.30pm. Oldham Council's Director of Communities Neil Consterdine said: "The Feast of Fire is one of the most exciting events in our calendar during Oldham's year as the Greater Manchester Town of Culture — and it's completely free. "We're looking forward to welcoming families or an unforgettable evening of entertainment, and with free parking from 3.30pm, it's the perfect opportunity to come into town, enjoy the Halloween night fun and support our local businesses while you're here." candidates.evidence_text: From the fabulous Feast of Fire celebrations to the iconic Christmas Lights Switch-On, the town centre will host an exciting calendar of entertainment as the Greater Manchester Town of Culture 2026. The programme will showcase the very best of Oldham's culture, creativity and community spirit with a series of free family-friendly events. The programme begins with the Feast of Fire event on Saturday 31 October 2026. A joint celebration of Halloween and Bonfire Night, this spellbinding event will light up the heart of the town centre with fire dance performances and The Lips Halloween Show by Puppets with Guts followed by a pyrotechnic Halloween fireworks display in the area around Parliament Square from 5.30pm. Then, just two weeks later, the festive season will officially begin with the Oldham Christmas Lights Switch-On event on Saturday 14 November, starting from 1pm. The day will feature meet and greets with Peppa Pig, appearances from Oldham's mascots and activities by the Spindles Kids Club. The celebrations will continue into the evening with the big Switch On Show from 5.30pm featuring Father Christmas, Peppa Pig's Dance Party, Oldham Rock Choir and performances from Fierce Dance. The Mayor of Oldham Cllr Pam Byrne will also take part in the celebrations before a local school child competition winner will switch on the town's Christmas lights. The evening will conclude with a festive fireworks finale, accompanied by a lights and laser show. To coincide with the switch on, the Festive Fun with Peppa Cinema Experience is coming to the Odeon at Parliament Square on Saturday 14 and Sunday 15 November, at 10am and 11.30am both days. Join Peppa Pig and her family at the cinema for a festive big-screen experience as they celebrate Evie’s first Christmas. To book click here. The following weekend, on Saturday 12 December, the town centre will be transformed for Winter Wonderland Saturday. candidates.evidence_text: An exciting new visitor attraction has opened its doors in the heart of Oldham. The first phase of Northern Roots is now open, marking an exciting chapter at the home of what will be the UK’s largest urban farm. Delivered through a partnership between the Northern Roots charity and Oldham Council, the new 160-acre development gives people the chance to enjoy nature closer to home, improving local health and wellbeing, supporting education, creating local jobs, and playing an important role in Oldham's ongoing regeneration. The project is transforming 160-acres of underused land next to Alexandra Park into a landmark destination, and the opening day gave visitors their first opportunity to experience the Welcome Building, cafe, Forestry Skills Centre, Urban Farm, and an expanding network of trails, orchards, woodland and wetlands. Thousands of visitors from across Oldham and beyond flocked to the site to experience Oldham’s newest major visitor attraction. Families enjoyed an outdoor play area with a sandpit, climbing frames and water play, and free activities including face painting, outdoor games, live music, a bubble performer, unicyclist and roaming stilt walkers. They could explore Snipe Clough Farm, a new four-acre working urban farm, and make wildflower seed bombs with the friendly team of volunteers. One family, who travelled over from Stockport for the opening, said: "It's really nice to see sustainable projects like this. It's a great day out for the family." And Sami Al-Othman from Stretford said: "It's great. This is what's needed everywhere. We're always looking for new things to do with the kids so this is perfect." The new cafe menu has been developed with acclaimed chef, food writer and restaurateur Mary-Ellen McTague – a 'farm-to-fork experience' serving fresh ingredients straight from the farm. Developed over the past five years, Northern Roots includes spaces for school visits, community events, meetings, exhibitions and performances. By 2030, Northern Roots aims to attract 300,000 visitors a year. candidates.lead: Oldham Council has approved a new package of interim governance arrangements
candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Council has approved a new package of interim governance arrangements. These measures are designed to strengthen democratic oversight, provide clear political leadership across key service areas and support transparent decision-making while the borough continues to work towards the appointment of a Council Leader and Cabinet. The arrangements were approved by Council on 16 September and include the creation of interim Lead Member and Deputy Lead Member roles aligned to the Council's four directorates. The arrangements form part of a wider governance framework developed following legal advice, engagement with the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, and discussions between political group leaders. Under the arrangements, Chief Executive Shelley Kipling will continue to exercise delegated executive powers, while Lead Members provide political oversight, advocacy and a visible link between residents, councillors and services. The roles carry no executive decision-making powers. The four Interim Lead Member portfolios have been allocated to the Council's four largest political groups, with deputy roles assigned from the same groups. Interim Lead Member appointments Resources - Lead Member: Sam Al-Hamdani (Liberal Democrats) - Deputy Lead Member: Mark Kenyon (Liberal Democrats) The Resources portfolio will provide political oversight of the Council's finances, budget management, transformation programme, corporate services, governance, workforce and organisational performance. Place - Lead Member: Arooj Shah (Labour) - Deputy Lead Member: Elaine Taylor (Labour) The Place portfolio will focus on regeneration, economic growth, planning, housing, highways, environmental services, transport and the continued delivery of major projects that support Oldham's future prosperity. Children and Young People - Lead Member: Mark Wilkinson (Reform UK) - Deputy Lead Member: Gary Tarbuck (Reform UK) The Children and Young People portfolio will provide oversight and advocacy for children's social care, education, safeguarding, special educational needs and early help services. The Lead Member will also undertake the statutory Lead Member role for children's services as far as practicable within the interim arrangements. candidates.evidence_text: Rochdale Town Hall’s Martlet Kitchen has picked up the Trip Advisor Travellers’ Choice Award 2026, placing it among the top-rated restaurants in the world on the popular review site The award honours businesses which consistently receive great reviews, with their scores placing them in the top 10 per cent of all establishments registered on the popular review site With millions of businesses from around the globe listed on the site, the award is a huge accolade for the Martlet Kitchen, which recently celebrated its second birthday It’s not the first time the restaurant, which specialises in traditional, high-quality British food, has been lauded In his food column for The Guardian, legendary food critic Jay Rayner, described the Martlet Kitchen as a ‘victory of professionalism, good sense and, most of all, great taste and skill’ when he visited shortly after its opening in 2024 The Martlet Kitchen is helmed by multi award winning chef, Darren Parkinson, who trained at Hopwood Hall College before working at acclaimed establishments including Shibden Mill Inn in Halifax and the Fleece Inn in Ripponden, both of which boast 2 AA rosettes

candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . candidates.lead: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians.
candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

candidates.evidence_text: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club, or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! Across this 5 day course, we’ll be exploring music for film, and working on composing music for the silent film ‘A Trip to the Moon’. The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. You can bring your own instruments, but we have keyboards, guitars, bass, violins, drums and percussion on site which can be used if you don’t have an instrument. Please email learning@bandonthewall.org if you have any questions about this course

The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. You can bring your own instruments, but we have keyboards, guitars, bass, violins, drums and percussion on site which can be used if you don’t have an instrument. Please email learning@bandonthewall.org if you have any questions about this course

candidates.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. They are now, by his assessment, considerably less so. Downstairs has been redone, upstairs has new ones too, while a previously overlooked back room has been completely reworked

They started with UK field sales as a proof of concept initially

The partnership is a significant expansion of last year’s collaboration, which saw Leonard and Manc At The Forest Side in Grasmere, Leonard is renowned for his creative, ingredient-led approach to modern British cuisine, drawing inspiration from the Cumbrian landscape and its seasonal produce, including ingredients grown and foraged from the restaurant’s 45-acre grounds Under his leadership, the restaurant has retained its Michelin Star, first awarded in 2016, and was awarded a Michelin Green Star earlier this year in recognition of its commitment to sustainability and ingredient provenance. The hotel also received a Michelin Key in 2024 The initiative has been championed by Manchester Art Fair Executive Chair Thom Hetherington, who was previously involved in the launch of Restaurant magazine and The World’s 50 Best Restaurants Awards

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester will mark Remembrance Sunday with its annual city centre service this November Honouring the service and sacrifice of members of the Armed Forces community, the commemorative event is open to all and will take place on Sun 8 Nov at the Manchester Cenotaph in St Peter’s Square between 10.30am and 12pm At 10.30am veterans, serving military personnel and cadets, led by the Greater Manchester Police Band, will march from John Dalton Street to the Cenotaph At 10.45am, the civic procession will set off from Mount Street, accompanied by the Scots Guards Association Pipe Band, making its way to the Cenotaph ahead of the service At 10.58am, the service will begin. A two-minute silence will be observed at 11am in tribute to those who have lost their lives in conflict. The start and conclusion of the silence will be marked by the firing of a maroon Following the service, veterans, military personnel and cadets will take part in a short return march across St Peter’s Square to Mount Street

From years spent languishing in post-industrial decline to being crowned one of ‘the coolest neighbourhoods in the world’ in the blink of an eye. What’s the story here? Find out with Jonathan Schofield Tours, with whom you’ll track Ancoats’ changes by strolling its streets, crossing its canals, and taking a look inside one of its most fascinating buildings Starting at Cutting Room Square, your expert tour guide will reveal the layers of history that make Ancoats special, from its place in establishing Manchester’s reputation as ‘Cottonopolis’ to the notorious street gangs, or ‘scuttlers’, who once patrolled and fought here But this winsome stroll is also about the urban regeneration and cultural energy of Ancoats today, which boasts everything from grassroots theatres to Manchester’s only Michelin-starred restaurant

This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

candidates.evidence_text: Lowry , Salford 4 November 2026 Additional information Always double check opening hours with the venue before making a special visit Few songs are quite as instantly associated with Greater Manchester as Brian and Michael’s 1978 hit ‘Matchstalk Men and Matchstalk Cats and Dogs’. Written about the life and paintings of L. S. Lowry, it turned one of the region’s best-known artists into an unlikely pop culture ph Coming to Lowry this November, Matchstalks Remastered is a playful music-theatre performance inspired by the song, the artist and the city that connects them. Two performers, accompanied by live jazz musician Adam Fairhall and a record player, attempt to follow a constantly scrol As the record plays, movement, storytelling and slapstick collide. Kevin Egan and Michael Pinchbeck shift between performers, songwriters, Lowry himself and the familiar figures populating his paintings, using the structure of the original song to create a series of theatrical sc Along the way, the production follows Lowry’s footsteps around Manchester and plays with the way stories about artists are remembered and retold. How does a painting become a song? What happens when that song becomes theatre? And what gets lost, exaggerated or reinvented along th The performance also arrives in the year marking the 50th anniversary of Lowry’s death, offering an appropriately unconventional way to revisit an artist whose industrial landscapes remain closely tied to the identity of Greater Manchester

Eat, meet, drink, shop, watch, talk, listen, laugh. Come in, be yourself and if you like it bring your friends! Altrincham’s charter dates back to 1290, it’s location at the intersection of the Cheshire farm belt and the commercial commuter zone of Manchester means the town has a long and important history. candidates.lead: Bolton Car Boot Sale at Bolton Car Boot Sale
candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. Martinez has not held back on his thoughts on the situation , hitting out at the board following last month's Champions League Despite being punished for the comments by the club, Martinez kept his place in the starting line-up for the draw vs Leeds. Michael Carrick will be in charge of the team for tonight's home clash against AS Roma, despite the continued pressure on the United boss United will be looking to get back to winning ways. A 2-0 defeat against Chelsea on Saturday means that the team are winless in their last nine games in all competitions It's led to a lot of questions being asked over the future of Carrick, although reports suggest that the situation will be reviewed during this month's international break. Following the game vs Roma, United host Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday (4.30pm kick-off) Former Newcastle United manager Eddie Howe has been named as a potential option for United, should they opt to make a change. candidates.evidence_text: 8 ноября 2026 года в Indigo at The O2 состоится концерт GORAN BREGOVIC в Лондоне Имя Горана Бреговича давно стало символом целого музыкального мира. Его путь начался в многонациональном Сараеве, где восточные мотивы естественно переплетались с западными традициями, а каждая улица имела свой ритм. Именно эта атмосфера сформировала композитора, впоследствии воз Впоследствии музыка Бреговича вышла за рамки концертных площадок. Сотрудничество с режиссером Emir Kusturica подарило мировому кинематографу саундтреки, ставшие неотъемлемой частью фильмов Time of the Gypsies, Arizona Dream и Underground. В этих мелодиях живут Балканы — с их своб Популярность Бреговича родилась не только благодаря знаменитым композициям “Kalashnikov”, “Ederlezi”, “In the Death Car” или “Bella Ciao”. Его главный талант — превращать народные мотивы в современное искусство, не теряя их подлинной силы. Вместе с легендарным “Wedding and Funera Окунитесь в этот балканский водоворот прямо в самом сердце Лондона! Город, который веками принимал выступления и разные культуры со всех континентов, на один вечер станет местом встречи британской сдержанности и безудержной балканской страсти. После выхода хита «Kasaba» в 2008 году Мурат Далкылыч стал одной из главных фигур турецкой поп-музыки. Он известен своим узнаваемым голосом, энергичными выступлениями и популярными песнями, среди которых «Bir Güzellik Yap». За годы карьеры в музыке, написании песен и кино он приобрел большую и преданную аудиторию как в Турции, так и за ее пределами. 29 января 2027 года Мурат Далкылыч выступит в indigo at The O2 в Лондоне. Вас ждет яркий вечер турецкой поп-музыки, живого исполнения и любимых хитов. Не упустите возможность увидеть Мурата Далкылыча вживую в Лондоне! Предварительный заказ
